clues: This city stands by the wide mouth of a great river in Colombia, near the warm Caribbean Sea. It is the biggest city on that coast of the country.
Trade winds cool this hot city from late fall to spring each year. Then two rainy times come, and rain can turn some streets into streams.
This town was set up by law in 1813, though folks lived here long before. It soon grew into a port where ships came and went.
Its big street party is one of the top folk fairs in the land. UNESCO named it a world treasure of culture in 2003.
The airport here was built in 1919, the first airport in all of South America. Planes from home and far lands still land there each day.
